bias: Markets are closed for the weekend, but the RRP buffer's slide to $0.25B — effectively fully exhausted — is the standout plumbing signal: any further reserve pressure now has no cushion left to absorb it. Vol and credit continue to hold their recent gains (MOVE flat near 69.6, VIX down another 2.6% to 14.26, credit proxies steady), and Korea/semis remain firm. But long yields ticked up again (10Y +0.92%, 30Y +0.80% on the week) and breakevens firmed a few bps alongside a second day of oil gains — a modest but real shift toward the inflation-reacceleration watch list. With Retail Sales now behind us and the next catalyst a month away (FOMC Sep 15-16), the tape has room to drift until fresh data arrives.

counterargs.read: With the RRP buffer now essentially exhausted, the plumbing has lost its main shock absorber — the next TGA draw or reserve drain will show up more directly rather than being cushioned. That's a structural concern sitting underneath a tape that otherwise looks calm: vol and credit are holding their gains, and there's no binary catalyst for a month. The modest firming in breakevens and oil is worth tracking, since it argues against the disinflation thesis at the margin even though it isn't yet a reversal.
